title: Replication and consistency
summary: Replication copies data across nodes, while consistency rules determine what reads can observe.
overview: Asynchronous replicas can lag committed writes and lose recent changes on failover. Synchronous acknowledgement strengthens specific durability guarantees, but read visibility depends on the acknowledgement mode and replica selected.
why: A successful write does not automatically mean every replica can return it immediately.
example: After saving a profile, an application reads it from the primary rather than a potentially lagging reporting replica.
judgment: Decide acceptable stale reads and data loss, then choose acknowledgement and routing behavior accordingly.
next: Does our acknowledgement wait for remote persistence or for changes to become queryable?
